High-Yield Topics: Reports and Indices are a cornerstone of the ESI paper and also appear in FM. They are used for both objective (passage-based and direct) and descriptive questions. 2. Types of Reports to Cover: o Indian Flagships: Union Budget and Economic Survey are non- negotiable. You must know their key themes, targets (fiscal deficit, GDP growth), and major allocations/new initiatives. o RBI Publications: Financial Stability Report (FSR), Report on Currency and Finance (RCF), and the RBI Annual Report are critical. o NITI Aayog Indices: SDG India Index and NITI Aayog Health Index are frequently asked. Know the top/bottom states and key parameters. o International "Big 4":  World Bank: World Development Report (WDR) (theme is vital for descriptive) and Ease of Doing Business (when it was published).  IMF: World Economic Outlook (WEO) and Global Financial Stability Report (GFSR) (especially India's GDP forecasts).  WEF: Global Gender Gap Report and Global Risks Report.  UNDP: Human Development Index (HDI), Gender Inequality Index (GII), and Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) (India's rank, parameters). o Key Committees (Finance): Any committee set up by RBI or the Ministry of Finance is crucial. The PYQs show a clear focus on N.K. Singh (FRBM), Bimal Jalan (ECF), P.J. Nayak (Bank Boards), and

# Page 5^page=5
Uday Kotak (Corporate Governance). Know their key recommendations. 3. How to Prepare Notes for Reports: o Publisher: Who releases it? (e.g., IMF, World Bank, NITI Aayog). o Frequency: Annual, Biennial, etc. o Theme/Title: What was the main theme? (e.g., WDR 2023 was "Migrants, Refugees and Societies"). o Key Findings (Global): What was the main global takeaway? o India-Specific Findings:  Rank: India's rank in the index (if any).  Top/Bottom: Top 3 and Bottom 3 countries/states.  Data Points: India's specific score, GDP forecast, or any key data point mentioned (e.g., % of women in workforce). o Parameters: What are the main pillars/indicators used in the index? (e.g., HDI uses health, education, standard of living). o Recommendations: What are the key policy recommendations, especially for India? (Crucial for descriptive answers). 4. Sources: o Primary: PIB (for launch summaries), Official RBI/NITI Aayog/World Bank/IMF websites (download the executive summaries). o Secondary: Your coaching material (like the provided EduTap/Sunya docs) and current affairs magazines will consolidate this information for you. For your December 2025 exam, you must focus on the reports released from January 2025 onwards, with a special emphasis on the Union Budget 2025 and Economic Survey 2025.

Report: World Development Report (WDR) o 2024 (Objective):  The specific Director of the WDR 2024 (Somik V. Lall).  Key strategies recommended (e.g., "3i strategy," women in the workforce).  A specific statistic from the report (number of economies that transitioned from middle- to high-income).  Specific findings related to India (e.g., time to reach US income levels, firm size growth). o 2023 & 2022 (Descriptive):  Based on the WDR 2023: Migrants, Refugees and Societies.  The question asked for an elaboration of the report's main theme ("Better migration policies for a prospering World") and its key recommendations. o 2017 (Objective):  Based on the 'India Development Report'.  A specific statistic (participation of women in the workforce). 2. Report: Human Capital Index o 2022 (Objective):

 Findings on implementation (more complicated than anticipated).  Report: CRY Report o 2017 (Objective):  A specific statistic (people without access to clean drinking water). Summary of Question Types from Reports Across all years, the questions asked from reports fall into these distinct categories: 1. Releasing Body: Who publishes the report? (e.g., WEO, GFSR, HDI, SEQI). 2. Specific Statistics/Data: o Growth Rates: India's GDP projection, global growth projection. o Ranks: India's rank in an index (e.g., HCI, GII). o Targets/Limits: FPI limits (15%), UPI limits (5 lakh), committee composition (1/3), SDG indicators (19/33). o Key Figures: Number of people (lifted from poverty), number of economies (transitioned), financial allocations. 3. Key Concepts & Definitions: o The formal name of a commission (Brundtland). o The definition of a term used by the report (Polycrisis). o The "5 Ps" of the SDG movement. 4. Parameters & Frameworks: o The parameters of an index (HCI, GII). o The guiding framework for an index (SDG India Index -> NIF). o The pillars of a framework (Basel III).

Recommendations & Findings (Qualitative): o Objective: Reasons for a ranking change, reasons for downward growth revision, key risks identified. o Descriptive: Key recommendations (WDR 2023), macroeconomic effects (RBI RCF), actions India can take (UNDP GSNI). 7.
